name: gdc-cgci-htmcp-lc
alternateName: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Lung Cancer
description:
People living with HIV have substantially elevated lung cancer incidence and worse outcomes, and are close to absent from the cohorts that define lung cancer genomics. This is the smallest cohort we have made a showcase page for, and we included it because size is not the only thing that determines whether a dataset is worth knowing about.
All 39 cases carry whole genome sequencing, 38 RNA sequencing and 37 microRNA. 26 patients are recorded as Black or African American. Pathologic stage is recorded for 62% and prior treatment for 92%, both unusually good for a cohort of this size.
citeAs: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Lung Cancer

supportedQuestions: Does lung cancer arising in people living with HIV differ genomically from lung cancer in the general population?
Can this cohort serve as a validation set for HIV-associated cancer hypotheses?
What is the survival experience of this population?

blockingLimitations.statement: 39 cases is the smallest cohort with a showcase page here. Nearly every analysis is underpowered, and no subgroup analysis is viable.
HIV status, CD4 count and antiretroviral history are not structured fields. Progression and last known disease status are empty for all cases.

inappropriateUses: Comparing HIV-positive with HIV-negative patients within the cohort.
